key_insight: Reliable protein–ligand binding prediction requires trustworthy evaluation, not just strong benchmark scores. The authors advocate transparent data, code and experimental procedures to make comparisons fair and reproducible.
problem_solved: Data leakage, biased benchmarks and unclear evaluation procedures can inflate reported performance and obscure which scoring methods genuinely generalize.
method: Promote transparency in datasets, code and experimental procedures.
Discuss good practices for preventing data leakage and bias during evaluation.
Encourage consistent, reproducible comparisons across protein–ligand scoring methods.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, these guidelines help distinguish genuine predictive gains from evaluation artifacts. More rigorous benchmarking supports better-informed model selection for protein–ligand binding prediction.
visual_elements: Protein–ligand binding illustration showing a molecule fitting into a protein pocket.
Train–test split diagram with a warning symbol highlighting data leakage.
Transparency checklist with icons for data, code and experimental procedures.
Side-by-side evaluation pipelines contrasting biased benchmarking with fair, reproducible comparison.
paper_title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction
